name: Mysore Masala Dosa
steps: Soak rice, urad dal and fenugreek separately for 5 hours. Grind with the soaked poha and enough measured water into a smooth pourable batter. Cover loosely and ferment overnight until bubbly; then stir in half the salt.
For the red chutney, soak dried chillies in hot water and blend with garlic, roasted chana dal and a little of the measured water to a thick spreadable paste.
Heat 20 ml oil, splutter mustard and curry leaves, soften chopped onion, then add turmeric, mashed boiled potato and remaining salt. Cook until the filling is hot and fairly dry.

Spread a ladle of fermented batter thinly on a hot griddle. Drizzle some remaining oil around it, cook until the base turns golden, then smear a thin layer of red chutney and a little butter across the top.

Place potato masala down the middle, fold the dosa around it and cook briefly until crisp. Repeat for four large dosas and serve at once; keep the chutney layer thin so it does not overpower the filling.
tips: The red chutney belongs inside the dosa; apply it only after the underside has set.
passiveTime: Soak rice and dal for 5 hours; ferment the batter overnight.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
